statusDefinitions.implemented: Behavior exists and has an automated test for the stated scope.
statusDefinitions.partial: Behavior exists for a bounded subset; the limitation and evidence are listed.
statusDefinitions.planned: Not advertised. Follow-up work is recorded below.
statusDefinitions.unavailable: The active 0.1.1 toolchain or packaged providers do not provide this behavior.

advertisingRule: A capability is advertised only when advertised is true and evidence is non-empty. Partial capabilities must display their scope and limitation in Vitte: Show Capabilities.

editorFeatures.label: Status, project actions and accessible editor UI
editorFeatures.description: The status item reports language-server readiness, active compiler verification and project diagnostics. Native quick picks expose compiler, project and target workflows. Theme colors and static status indicators follow VS Code theme and reduced-motion preferences; no Vitte keybindings override editor shortcuts.
editorFeatures.limitation: English and French cover the status item, project/compiler/target pickers, module view and diagnostic summaries/views. Other legacy strings, command titles and compiler/server messages may remain untranslated. Automated keyboard, screen-reader and high-contrast regression coverage is not recorded, so the broader UX capability is not advertised as complete.

editorFeatures.label: Project detection, toolchains and build tasks
editorFeatures.provider: VS Code extension and Vitte CLI
editorFeatures.description: Detects the nearest CLI-supported vitte.toml or .vitte/config file, runs Check/Build/Run on the active source through the selected CLI, applies folder-scoped compiler arguments, environment, target and manifest settings, forwards module roots through VITTE_MODULE_PATH, and generates extension-owned task templates. A separate explicit Build Compiler Repository task uses Make; Test is offered only when that checkout has an actual Make test target.
editorFeatures.limitation: Compiler-repository Make tasks report an error when a Vitte project config or CLI-only target, manifest or compiler arguments would otherwise be ignored. The LSP does not infer package/generated-source mappings from manifests. The CLI 0.1.1 has no reliable test discovery metadata or structured results, so Test Explorer discovery/run/debug actions are unavailable. The experimental native DAP template requires explicit opt-in and is limited to Linux x86_64 / Ubuntu 24.04; external DAP adapters remain available elsewhere.

editorFeatures.label: Completion
editorFeatures.description: Contextual completions for lexical bindings, keywords, declared types, form fields, pick variants, callable declarations and values, attributes, filesystem module/import paths, explicitly imported exports, and trait methods with a visible implementation or generic trait bound.
editorFeatures.limitation: The active compiler has no editor semantic-query API. Results are parsed from a bounded source subset, so overload resolution and inferred receiver types are unavailable; direct inherent impl methods and type-qualified associated functions are not advertised because the active frontend does not validate them. Trait method suggestions require a visible trait plus a source-detected implementation or bound. Named procedure-call arguments are not in the active grammar. Missing module roots and unresolved typed receivers show a non-inserting status item. Files over 512 KiB use a lightweight keyword/builtin fallback; disk enumeration and module reads are bounded.

editorFeatures.label: Native debugging
editorFeatures.provider: Bundled DAP adapter with LLDB and DWARF
editorFeatures.description: An explicitly enabled experimental LLDB/DAP backend compiles source with --debug-info and #line mappings or launches an existing executable whose DWARF names Vitte sources. editorFeatures.limitation: Requires Vitte CLI 0.1.1, LLDB and Expect on Linux x86_64 / Ubuntu 24.04. It is not advertised by default. The legacy extension-dap workflow still checks out a pinned older extension revision (98470ad8de948a4fb3ecdc8c41e2a4c7ee66b441), so it does not validate native DAP on this 2.3.10 source snapshot; the new cross-platform job verifies package activation only. On the active macOS arm64 host, compiling with --debug-info produced a Mach-O executable whose .debug_info and .debug_line sections were empty; local DAP scenarios also fail frame, variable and breakpoint checks. Windows has no native DAP gate. Source mapping relies on C #line/DWARF for source files emitted by the current backend; structured runtime diagnostics and generated multi-module source maps are unavailable.

followUps.description: Replace source-index approximations with compiler symbol/type/reference data for workspace symbols, cross-module navigation, semantic token identities, code lenses and inlay hints; add generated-target and hierarchy queries with parity tests before expanding their advertised scope.

followUps.label: Add compiler-backed completion and signature queries
followUps.description: Expose scope, type, visibility, overload and signature data from the active compiler frontend before expanding beyond the tested source-derived completion subset; decide whether named procedure-call arguments belong to the language grammar.

followUps.label: Implement or explicitly retire native test and formatter commands
followUps.description: The native driver rejects `vitte test` and `vitte fmt` and exposes no test metadata. Keep Test Explorer discovery/execution and document/range formatting unavailable until the compiler provides stable result contracts and parity evidence.

followUps.label: Expose canonical package and generated-source mappings to editor tooling
followUps.description: Add a compiler/CLI project query for source roots, package roots and generated Vitte files; until then, LSP navigation accepts explicit vitte.modulePaths only and does not infer package or generated-source mappings from manifests.

followUps.label: Close compiler platform and cross-target gates
followUps.description: Resolve and rerun Linux x86_64, macOS arm64 and Windows x86_64 release gates; publish no wider platform claim until toolchain jobs pass.

followUps.label: Move inline suggestions behind verified language-server results
followUps.description: Keep local n-gram/template and AI suggestion engines opt-in and experimental until outputs are validated against compiler/LSP semantics and stale candidates are rejected.

followUps.label: Gate the current native debugger build in CI
followUps.description: Run the checked-in extension and DAP regression scenarios against the exact compiler/extension revisions in CI, then resolve macOS 0.1.1 regressions and add Windows coverage before widening platform support or advertising the bundled native debugger by default.

followUps.label: Add canonical Vitte source maps and runtime debug events
followUps.description: Expose compiler source-map metadata and structured runtime failure locations to DAP for generated code and multi-module programs. Until then, source mapping uses C #line/DWARF entries and runtime exception reporting is limited to native signals.

followUps.label: Add symbol-proven import actions and safe refactorings
followUps.description: Expose import usage, visibility and unique destination data from the active compiler before implementing organize/remove-unused imports, add-import or qualification actions beyond exact compiler-marked machine-applicable suggestions.

followUps.label: Add request lifecycle and cross-platform workspace regressions
followUps.description: Add automated tests for cancellation and stale-result rejection across document edits, settings changes, file watcher events, workspace-folder changes and toolchain restarts; cover bounded queues, cache invalidation, symlink loops, URI escaping, non-ASCII paths and Windows/macOS case behavior.
